title: 3.5.21 Chart the Code: Destructuring vs. Plain Access
description: Chart a function whose body destructures its parameter, and see the unpack as its own task before the work that uses it.

aiGrader.prompt: This chart is scored entirely by rules from its shapes and arrows. No model reads it.

rubric.title: The unpack, then the note, then the decision
rubric.description: Scored by the editor (arrow order): the unpack task, then the task that builds the note, come before the decision on every route.

steps.fail: The unpack is its own task, drawn first: one box that takes width, height and color out of options (not a box that reads options.width). Then build the note in its own task, before the decision.
steps.pass: The unpack, then the note, then the decision.

steps.fail: Take all three values out of options in one task. A separate box for each field is plain access, one value at a time.
steps.pass: No task reads a single field out of options.

rubric.title: The wide path adds to the note
rubric.description: Scored by the editor: the decision has two different exits, and the yes exit goes to the task that adds to the note.

steps.fail: The yes arrow must lead to the task that appends to the note, and the no arrow to somewhere different.
steps.pass: The yes arrow goes to the task that adds to the note.

rubric.title: The print comes after the decision
rubric.description: Scored by the editor: an input/output step for the print, after the decision.

steps.fail: Both paths finish at one print. Draw an input/output step for the print.
Both paths must meet at the print, and the print must come after the decision, before End.
steps.pass: Both paths meet at the print before End.

rubric.title: The decision compares width and height
rubric.description: Scored by the editor: a diamond asks whether the width is greater than the height (or whether the box is wide).

steps.fail: The diamond should ask whether the width is greater than the height, so that yes is the wide case (not "or equal", and not the negated question).
steps.pass: The diamond compares width and height.

gate.fail: None of your shapes say what this program does. Label each shape in your own words.
